data.name: MachiaVillain
data.detailed_description:
Welcome to Villain City, a luxury community entrenched in the hills of horror. Ax murderers, mad scientists and tax evaders, all kinds of bad guys consider this place to be their sweet home. This is the perfect place to rest, relax, and pursue a career in the noblest of professions: professional Villain!!

The real estate agent promised you a haunted house with jump scare devices and terrifying traps. Instead, you have a piece of empty land full of Vermin near a rubbish forest.

But do not flee yet! With a little elbow grease, the help of your minions and a lot of murders, you can turn this house into a happy and dreary mortal trap. Just lure locals inside, then trigger your deadly traps or let your minion feast on their brains and flesh. Every night you'll multiply your evil level until everyone calls your mansion " scary, nasty and horrible."

Be aware that the League of MachiaVillain Villains has adopted a strict policy that governs the level of wickedness that you have to adhere to in order to stay in the community. Drs Frank and Stein, Siamese co-Chairmen of the Board of evil ( BDM ), dictated a series of rules to follow when conducting your villainous business. They cover everything from how to kill intruders- to what salads are considered the most evil (no surprise, grated carrots).

Follow the rules of the League and become the scariest neighborhood Villain!


  • Build your mansion: Create the evil mansion of your nightmares! Put together the perfect crypt for your vampire, the insanest lab for your mad scientist, an irresistible swimming pool for your victims (and your shark) and don't forget the cannibal kitchen!
  • Gather your evil nightmare team: Choose your minions wisely though, as each possesses different traits and have different needs that must be tended to. They also have different fighting styles, such as long range, bare handed, and of course, bare fanged.
  • Manage your monsters: No evil mansion is complete without a cadre of minions to keep it running. Order them to do your evil deeds, and don’t forget to have them clean the blood stains.
  • Slaughter innocent victims…and bankers!: Our menu tonight includes a wide array of victims from famous tropes such as jocks, nerds, potheads, party girls or horror movie celebrities. A good variety ensures your minions stay well-fed.
  • Fight all the things: The environment is full of hostile creatures who want to take your place at the top of the food chain. Chupacabra, Wendigo, Sasquatch... There are also pro monster hunters who come knocking at your door with stakes, holy water or baseball bats. Show them who's the boss… the Villain boss!
  • Bloody good crafting: Sawing through countless victims means you'll end up with a few spare parts. Why not use those bits and bobs to craft something useful? MachiaVillain lets you create things using ingredients gathered from victims and harvested from the environment. Put them together and you'll get something horrifying, but also useful.
  • Follow the Rules!:The key to evil survival in MachiaVillain is to follow the unspoken rules of the horror movie genre. You do have an Evil Mastermind Reputation to think about after all. Follow the villain's rules to be a real success. So slaughter them when they're alone, kill the virgin last, and never, ever hurt the dog!

data.short_description: Machiavillain is an evil mansion management and strategy game, inspired by Dungeon Keeper, Prison Architect and all the horror movie clichés! Build your own manor, raise your monsters, set up your traps, and exterminate your victims. But to gain reputation you'll have to slay by the horror movie rules!

Inglês*, Francês, Alemão, Português (Brasil), Russo
*idiomas com suporte total de áudio

reviews.review:
MachiaVillain offers a wonderfully unconventional approach to management simulation by allowing players to become the mastermind behind a sinister mansion rather than the hero attempting to escape one. Developed by Wild Factor and published by Good Shepherd Entertainment, this horror-themed strategy game combines base construction, resource management, monster recruitment, and dark comedy into an experience inspired by classic horror films. Released on May 16, 2018, it distinguishes itself through an imaginative premise that encourages players to embrace their villainous ambitions while maintaining an efficiently operated household of supernatural creatures. Although its creativity is immediately appealing, several mechanical shortcomings prevent it from fully realizing its considerable potential.

The adventure begins with a modest piece of property that must gradually be transformed into an intimidating mansion of nightmares. Players gather construction materials, establish essential facilities, and design rooms that serve both practical and murderous purposes. The building system offers considerable freedom, allowing experimentation with corridors, specialized chambers, decorations, and deadly traps. Every architectural decision contributes to the efficiency of the estate, especially when attracting unsuspecting visitors into carefully arranged ambushes. Watching an ordinary structure evolve into a functioning horror establishment delivers genuine satisfaction, although the construction interface occasionally becomes frustrating when handling complicated layouts.

Managing supernatural servants forms another essential component of the experience. Players recruit monsters with different capabilities and assign them responsibilities involving construction, harvesting, maintenance, and combat. These creatures are more than disposable workers because they require food, rest, and suitable accommodations to remain productive. Maintaining an effective workforce demands careful organization, particularly when several activities compete for attention. Unfortunately, the artificial intelligence does not always cooperate with the player's intentions. Workers sometimes struggle with navigation, inefficient priorities, or unfinished assignments, introducing unnecessary complications into otherwise enjoyable management mechanics.

The most entertaining feature involves eliminating visitors according to recognizable horror movie conventions. Rather than rewarding indiscriminate violence, the game encourages players to follow specific cinematic traditions when arranging murders. Victims should ideally be isolated before being attacked, certain individuals must survive until the appropriate moment, and harming innocent animals is strongly discouraged. Following these rules improves the player's reputation within the villainous community, adding an amusing strategic dimension to every encounter. This mechanic successfully transforms familiar horror clichés into meaningful gameplay considerations, making careful planning more rewarding than simply overwhelming visitors with monsters.

Resource gathering and crafting establish an interconnected economy that supports the mansion's continued expansion. Players must collect materials, produce equipment, manage supplies, and transform the remains of unfortunate guests into resources for their monstrous workforce. The resulting production cycle creates an entertaining relationship between construction, survival, and murder. However, maintaining this economy can become repetitive as the estate grows. Resource shortages, inefficient task assignments, and constant supervision occasionally interrupt the momentum, making some later stages feel more like administrative work than imaginative villainy.

Defensive planning becomes increasingly important when dangerous opponents begin investigating the property. Monster hunters and other hostile visitors can threaten the entire operation, requiring players to prepare traps, position servants strategically, and maintain an effective defensive layout. Successfully defeating enemies through carefully designed ambushes can be satisfying, but combat itself lacks substantial tactical depth. Limited unit control and unpredictable behavior sometimes reduce the effectiveness of thoughtful preparation. Consequently, the defensive mechanics are entertaining in concept but less consistently rewarding in execution.

The visual presentation embraces a colorful, cartoon-inspired aesthetic that contrasts effectively with the game's gruesome subject matter. Its exaggerated monsters, peculiar decorations, and distinctive environments establish a playful atmosphere rather than conventional horror. The top-down perspective provides a useful overview of the estate, while the expanding collection of rooms and machinery creates a satisfying visual representation of progress. The soundtrack complements this personality with appropriately mischievous music and atmospheric effects. Nevertheless, visual clutter can make busy environments difficult to interpret, and the limited musical variety becomes noticeable during extended sessions.

Progression initially feels rewarding because new facilities, creatures, and defensive possibilities gradually expand the player's options. Experimenting with mansion designs and different management strategies provides reasonable replay value, particularly for enthusiasts of sandbox simulations. However, the experience becomes less compelling once its central systems are fully understood. Repetitive activities, awkward automation, and limited variety in long-term objectives diminish the excitement of expansion. The game would benefit considerably from more sophisticated artificial intelligence, additional strategic possibilities, and improved quality-of-life features.

Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, MachiaVillain currently has no confirmed Steam Deck Verified or Playable classification, so its compatibility should be considered Unknown or Unverified. Although the game supports Linux alongside Windows and macOS, native Linux availability does not automatically guarantee smooth operation on Valve's handheld. Its cursor-oriented interface and management-heavy controls may require customized controller layouts or extensive trackpad usage. Players primarily interested in handheld gaming should therefore approach the experience cautiously, particularly if they prefer games designed around conventional controller inputs.

Ultimately, MachiaVillain succeeds most convincingly through its originality, humorous personality, and entertaining interpretation of classic horror conventions. Constructing an elaborate mansion, commanding supernatural servants, and orchestrating cinematic murders provide a refreshing alternative to traditional management simulations. Unfortunately, inconsistent worker behavior, repetitive resource management, awkward controls, and underdeveloped combat prevent its strongest ideas from achieving their full potential. Despite these limitations, the game remains an enjoyable experience for players who appreciate unusual strategy concepts and are willing to overlook technical imperfections.

Its imaginative premise, charming presentation, and creative mansion-building mechanics make it worth exploring, particularly for fans of horror comedy and management simulations. While it lacks the refinement and long-term depth of the genre's strongest examples, its distinctive personality and entertaining villainous gameplay provide enough enjoyment to justify a recommendation for patient players who value creativity over mechanical perfection.

Rating: 7/10
